items.title: Understanding Integer Operations via Number Lines
items.explanation: Integers can be represented on a number line where rightward movement is positive (+) and leftward movement is negative (-). When adding integers, you start at zero, move according to the first number, then continue moving according to the second number. For example, if the first strike moves 5 units right (positive 5) and the second strike moves 7 units left (negative -7), the final position is calculated as 5 + (-7) = -2.

items.title: Using Tokens to Solve Integer Subtraction Problems
items.explanation: To solve subtraction problems like (+7) – (+18), use a token model where green tokens represent positive numbers and red tokens represent negative numbers. Start with 7 green tokens. To subtract 18, you must remove 18 positive tokens. Since there are only 7 available, add pairs of zero tokens (one green, one red) until you have enough to remove all 18 positives. After removing the positives, any remaining red tokens represent the answer.
